title: Solstice Utilities private deploy sketch
body:
Meeting notes + sketch for Solstice Utilities private deployment pilot (customer call 2025-11-03).

Meeting summary:
- Quick sync to map pilot goals, technical constraints, and MVP success criteria. Solstice is a regional utility provider planning to use LLMs for outage triage and routing to field crews. They need a private deployment (VPC) with strict data residency (US midwest) and an SLA for sub-200ms median synth latency on short prompts (instructions + meter id).

Attendees on call:
- Ivy Park (Solstice PM)
- Kenji Sato (Solstice infra lead)
- Luis Fernandez (Solstice SRE) - joined late
- Liam Rodriguez (Redwood solutions eng)
- Maya Ortiz (Redwood solutions eng)
- Rhea Kumar (Redwood AM)

Customer context and goals:
- Use-case: automated first-pass triage of outage reports via text and short form voice->transcript input. Outputs: classification, suggested dispatch code, suggested SLA bucket, and confidence score.
- Throughput: 40 qps peak, expected sustained 10 qps. Bursty during storms (spike factor ~6).
- Data residency: must run in their AWS account in us-east-2 (Ohio). No PHI, but personally identifiable info (addresses) must not leave their VPC.
- Uptime expectation for pilot: 99.5% monthly. If successful, will negotiate Dedicated reserved capacity.

Technical requirements (explicit):
1) Private control plane (managed by Redwood) + data plane in Solstice AWS account (VPC peering or PrivateLink). Customer prefers PrivateLink to avoid cross-account ENIs.
2) Model: start with a compact open model (quantized) we have perf data for on A100 80GB equivalent; fallback policy to a lower-cost variant if latency SLOs threatened.
3) KV cache / prefix caching: necessary because many queries reuse meter id context. Need guidance on TTL and cache invalidation when crew updates status.
4) Batching policy: small dynamic batching (max 8) with low-latency tail optimization; configure burst autoscaling for storm windows.
5) Logging: redacted request/response logging by default; optional full logging to Solstice S3 bucket with lifecycle rules.
6) Auth: mTLS for service-to-service, and integration with Solstice IdP for console access.
7) Monitoring: token-level latency histograms, per-route error rates, and quality regression alerts tied to a validation prompt set.

Gotchas, risks, and open issues:
- Network topology: Solstice's networking team requires explicit design doc for PrivateLink + NLB + ENI allocation. They are cautious about overlapping subnets (they have a legacy /16). Need to surface port requirements early.
- Cold start latency when autoscaling GPU nodes from 0 -> N can breach 2s; propose warm pool of 2 nodes for pilot. Cost vs SLA debate.
- Data sanitization: transcripts may contain PII (addresses). They want deterministic masking at ingestion. Need to confirm acceptable masking logic (hash vs redact) and retention policy.
- Model hallucination risk: for dispatch decisions, legal requirement says assistant cannot create new addresses or change critical fields. We must add structured output (dispatch_code, confidence) + deterministic validation layer before returning actionable suggestions.
- KV cache coherency: crew updates must invalidate cache TTL quickly. Integration point: webhook from their dispatch system to Redwood control plane to invalidate keys. Need sample event format.
- Capacity planning uncertainty: customer traffic estimates are hand-wavy. Ask for 7-day per-minute historic volumes for two storm events.
- Security: they may require HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest in production. Pilot can use KMS with RBAC, but plan for HSM later.

Immediate action items (who / by when):
- Maya: draft PrivateLink network layout diagram and required ports + NLB sizing (due 2025-11-10).
- Liam: provide config template for warm pool autoscaling + cost estimate (A100 equiv warm pool of 2 nodes vs keep 0 warm) (due 2025-11-07).
- Rhea: capture customer procurement timeline and procurement POC (due 2025-11-06).
- Ivy / Kenji: share 7-day minute-level traffic sample (anonymized) and example dispatch webhook schema (due 2025-11-10).
- Ethan: quick security note on KMS vs HSM tradeoffs and what triggers HSM requirement (due 2025-11-12).

MVP success criteria (for pilot sign-off):
- Avg end-to-end median latency < 200ms for the short prompt path (excluding ASR). 95th < 600ms under expected load.
- Classification accuracy > 88% on the curated validation set (they will share labeled 1k examples).
- No PII leaves customer VPC in unredacted form; logs stored only in their S3 bucket during pilot.
- Failover behavior: if inference cluster unhealthy, requests fallback to a lightweight on-prem model returning a safe fail response (structured error + note to escalate).

Notes on implementation choices (quick thoughts):
- Suggest starting with a 4-slot warm pool of mid-sized GPUs with our quantized 7B-ish variant (tradeoff: lower token cost, predictable latency). Use model variant routing by prompt_length and priority routes for critical paths.
- For caching, use prefix caching keyed on meter_id + recent event_hash. Default TTL 90s, with explicit invalidation via webhook on status change.
- Observability: add a per-request metadata blob including inbound source (mobile/app/web), meter_id hash, and route election reason to help debug SLO breaches.

Questions for customer to confirm on next call:
- Confirm allowed masking approach for address fields (redact vs pseudonymize) and whether pseudonyms must be reversible by Solstice only.
- Provide a small labeled validation set (250–1k) they are comfortable sharing for initial quality gating.
- Confirm which AWS account / role we will use for PrivateLink setup and whether they prefer CloudFormation or Terraform templates.

Longer term asks if pilot succeeds:
- Dedicated reserved pool (contracted), on-prem support for connective sites, HSM for production keying, and extended observability retention for compliance windows.

Misc notes (rough):
- They liked the fallback policy demo (canary -> region fallback) we showed.
- Ivy is sensitive to procurement timings: wants pilot kicked off before Q1 budget freeze.
- Keep the first pilot scope narrow: triage + suggested dispatch only (no automated dispatch).

Next meeting: schedule 2025-11-17 to review network diagram and initial perf/cost model.

---
Scratchpad ends here. Keep this doc informal; will turn into an internal runbook once we have traffic samples and network details.
